physics_scope: Geometric optics with opaque, specular bulk-Ti Fresnel walls; no phase-coherent interference, diffraction, near-field effects, roughness, oxide, or finite-film transfer.
M1 uses Ti on every face. M2 assumes a gray active face of alpha=0.90 with its specified reflection phase; this is not a fabricated or measured film.
Tabulated Ordal Ti optical data are not measured TA2 and are not validated at 523 K. Temperature is used for Planck spectral weighting only.
Absorptivity is interpreted as directional emissivity under reciprocity and an isothermal cell; walls contribute too. Neither model is qualified full-wave or experimental evidence.

A single normal-incidence azimuth fixes the tabulated s/p axes. In azimuth-integrated quantities, the polar endpoint is replaced by its exact polarization-trace average (s+p)/2; that unpolarized average is independent of transverse basis.
The largest sampled emissivity is not necessarily the direction of largest projected power and is not proof of a narrow lobe. No FWHM or precise beam-axis fit is claimed.

uncertainty_scope.mc_se: Per-result standard errors measure independent ray-position Monte Carlo variation. Aggregate SE is the sum of positive-weighted SE values, a conservative covariance bound rather than an independent-sample RSS estimate or a 95% interval.
uncertainty_scope.unresolved: Residual ray energy is a one-sided absorption bound and is never counted as escaped. It is reported separately from statistical sampling error.
uncertainty_scope.angular_spectral: Theta, azimuth and wavelength downsample comparisons are sensitivity indicators, not guaranteed error bounds. Geometry, material, ray-model bias and selected-peak bias are not covered by MC SE.
uncertainty_scope.horizon: The unobserved 89–90-degree hemisphere contributes at most cos(89 degrees)^2=0.0003045865 in absolute normalized hemispherical emissivity, assuming passive epsilon in [0,1].

metric_definitions.normal: Planck-weighted 8–13 um directional emissivity at theta=0
metric_definitions.hemisphere: integral epsilon(theta,phi)*cos(theta)*dOmega/pi; constant theta89 tail to90
metric_definitions.cone_fraction: integral of projected emitted power inside normal-axis cone divided by total hemisphere power
metric_definitions.cone_power: cone numerator normalized by whole-cell blackbody hemispheric band power
metric_definitions.power_peak: maximum sampled epsilon(theta,phi)*cos(theta); distinct from emissivity maximum
metric_definitions.FWHM: Not computed or inferred from the sampled maximum

emissivity_peak.interpretation: Sampled maximum; selection bias and finite-grid location error are not included in its MC SE. Not a fitted lobe or FWHM.

projected_power_peak.interpretation: Power per unit solid angle per projected cell area, normalized by blackbody radiance; not radiance/emissivity peak.

A0_A1_A2_A3.wall_shape: A0/A1/A2 CPC curves with128segments; A3 straight frustum walls

B.active_face: +x slanted face only; top and floor Ti

geometry.comparison_caution: A0/A3 have matched active and cell areas; B/C versus A-series also change active-area fraction and lattice area, so rankings include those choices.

ranking_cautions: Coarse-grid rank stability does not establish model validity or material accuracy.
M2 A0/A1 sampled peak magnitudes differ by less than their individual MC standard errors, so avoid a firm peak-emissivity ranking.
Normal 2.5-degree sample offset of A0 M2 from theta0 is not resolved given MC uncertainty; treat it as essentially normal-centered.
A3 has the greatest normal30 cone power fraction but A0 has the greatest normal15 cone fraction in M2; select by collection angle and absolute cone power together.
A1/A2 small emissivity peak shifts alone do not prove narrow off-axis emission. B M2 grazing emissivity peak differs from its projected-power peak.
Peak-centered spherical-cap membership on the angular grid has larger aliasing sensitivity than normal-axis cones, especially grazing peaks.
